titulo: I was, I could, I said
intro: Ten more verbs with an irregular indefinido: they share a new stem and endings with no accent.
p.estuve.consejo: The stem is «estuv-» and the ending has no accent: estuve, estuvo.
p.pude.consejo: «No pude» means you tried and did not manage it.
p.puse.consejo: The stem of «poner» is «pus-»: puse, puso, pusimos.
p.vine.consejo: The stem is «vin-»: vine, viniste, vino. Never «veni».
p.quise.consejo: With «no» it means «I refused»: «no quise ir» means you decided not to go.
p.supe.consejo: In the indefinido «saber» usually means «to find out»: «Supe la noticia».
p.dije.consejo: The j sounds like a strong h: «DI-he». It is the stem «dij-».
p.dijeron.consejo: After j the ending is -eron, not -ieron: dijeron, trajeron.
p.traje.consejo: «Traer» uses the stem «traj-»: traje, trajiste, trajo.
p.vi.consejo: «Vi» and «dio» have a single syllable: they take no accent.
p.la fiesta.consejo: You say «ir a la fiesta» and «venir a la fiesta». It is a feminine noun.
p.el regalo.consejo: You give it with «dar»: «di un regalo». The person goes with «le».
p.lo siento.consejo: It comes from «sentir». It is the usual polite phrase for apologising.
p.una tarta.consejo: In Spain you say «tarta»; in many Latin American countries, «torta» or «pastel».
b1.titulo: A new stem, endings with no accent
b1.texto:
Many common verbs change their stem in the indefinido:

- **estar** → **estuv-** (estuve, estuvo)
- **poder** → **pud-** (pude, pudo)
- **poner** → **pus-** (puse, puso)
- **venir** → **vin-** (vine, vino)
- **querer** → **quis-** (quise, quiso)
- **saber** → **sup-** (supe, supo)
- **decir** → **dij-** (dije, dijo)
- **traer** → **traj-** (traje, trajo)

They all use the same endings: **-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron**. **They take no accent**: estuve, pudo, vino.

With a stem in **j**, «ellos» takes **-eron**: **dijeron, trajeron**.

**Dar** and **ver** have short forms: **di, diste, dio** and **vi, viste, vio**, also with no accent.
b2.f0.texto: Why didn't you come to the party?
b2.f1.texto: I wanted to come but I couldn't.
b2.f3.texto: I was at the hospital with my mother.
b2.f7.texto: Everyone said the party was very fun.
b4.titulo: The endings of the irregular verbs
b4.texto:
With the new stem, the endings are always the same:

- **yo**: -e (estuve, pude)
- **tú**: -iste (estuviste, pudiste)
- **él, ella, usted**: -o (estuvo, pudo)
- **nosotros**: -imos (estuvimos, pudimos)
- **vosotros**: -isteis (estuvisteis, pudisteis)
- **ellos, ellas, ustedes**: -ieron (estuvieron, pudieron)

If the stem ends in **j** (dij-, traj-), «ellos» takes **-eron**: dijeron, trajeron.

Forms with an irregular stem **take no accent**, and the stress falls on the stem: **PU-so**, **ES-tu-vo**.

Watch the meaning: **no pude** means you tried, **no quise** means you decided not to, and **supe** means you found out.
b4.e1.texto: My cousins brought bread and fruit.
b4.e2.texto: I saw Ana at the party.
b5.f0.texto: That afternoon I was on the roof with a lemon cake.
b5.f1.texto: The sky laid pink clouds over the rooftops.
b5.f2.texto: The guests came up the stairs with laughter and with flowers.
b5.f3.texto: My uncle brought an old guitar of light wood.
b5.f4.texto: Nobody wanted to leave the roof.
b5.f5.texto: I saw Ana beside the window.
b5.f6.texto: She said my name in a soft and warm voice.
b5.f7.texto: I gave her a blue present.
b5.f8.texto: The cake tasted of honey and lemon.
b5.f9.texto: That night we made a promise under the stars.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! That gives pude, pudo, pudieron.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Pod-» is the stem of the infinitive, not of the indefinido.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Pued-» appears in the present: puedo, puedes. In the past it becomes «pud-».
b6.pregunta: Which stem does «poder» use in the indefinido?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Esté» is subjunctive, not a «yo» past form.
b7.pregunta: Complete with «estar» in the past, for «yo».
b8.frase: Ana trajo una tarta a la fiesta
b8.traduccion: Ana brought a cake to the party
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Poner» is irregular: it is not formed with -ió.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The stem is right, but these forms take no accent.
b9.pregunta: Which form of «poner» goes with «él» in the past?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes: after j, the ending is -eron.
b10.o1.refuerzo: After j the i is lost: it is -eron, not -ieron.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The stem of «decir» in the past is «dij-», not «dec-».
b10.pregunta: Complete with «decir» in the past, for «ellos».
b12.o0.refuerzo: That's it! In the indefinido «saber» usually means «to find out».
b12.o1.refuerzo: That would be «sabía», another past. «Supe» is the moment of finding out.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That would be «quise» or «quería». «Supe» does not mean wanting.
b12.pregunta: In «Supe la noticia anoche», what happened?
p.viniste.consejo: The stem of «venir» in the past is «vin-». For «tú»: «viniste», with no accent.
p.estuviste.consejo: The stem of «estar» in the past is «estuv-». For «tú»: «estuviste», with no accent.
p.divertida.consejo: It agrees with «fiesta»: feminine. The v sounds b; do not confuse it with «dividida».
p.trajeron.consejo: The stem «traj-» ends in j, so «ellos» takes -eron, not -ieron. The j sounds like a strong h.
p.azotea.consejo: Two strong vowels, e and a, are in different syllables: a-tho-TE-a. The z sounds «th» in Spain.
p.puso.consejo: The stem of «poner» in the past is «pus-» and there is no accent. The stress falls on the stem: PU-so.
p.rosadas.consejo: It agrees with «nubes»: feminine plural. The initial r is strong, like rr.
p.invitados.consejo: It comes from «invitar». A woman guest is «invitada». The v sounds b.
p.vinieron.consejo: Stem «vin-» plus -ieron. There is no accent. «Ie» is one syllable: bi-NYE-ron.
p.trajo.consejo: The stem is «traj-» and there is no accent: «trajo». The j sounds like a strong h.
p.quiso.consejo: The stem of «querer» in the past is «quis-». «Qui» sounds ki: KI-so. With «no», it means he refused.
p.dijo.consejo: The stem of «decir» in the past is «dij-». The j sounds like a strong h: DI-ho. No accent.
p.cálida.consejo: The accent marks the first syllable: KA-li-da. Masculine: «cálido». It agrees with «voz».
p.supo.consejo: «Saber a» means to taste of: «supo a miel». The stem in the past is «sup-», with no accent.
p.promesa.consejo: It comes from «prometer». «Hacer una promesa» means to make a promise. It is feminine.
p.pud.consejo: It is only a stem, not a whole word: «pud-» plus an ending gives «pude», «pudo», «pudieron».
p.enteró.consejo: It is used with «se»: «se enteró de la noticia». The accent marks the final stress.
